purpose: What a document says about the AI tools people may use and the data they may put into them: which kinds of tool are provided, approved, allowed or ruled out, which kinds of data may or may not be entered, what safeguards people are asked to apply, and which laws are named. Each row has a verbatim quote and a flag for whether the quote itself names AI. Rules about what AI may be used for are in the uses schema, and academic misconduct is in the misconduct schema.

tool_classes.institution_provided_tool: a tool or platform the institution supplies or licenses (for example Copilot, an in-house platform, a licensed edition)
tool_classes.approved_or_validated_tools: a list of approved, validated, supported or recommended tools, or a process for approving tools
tool_classes.external_or_consumer_tools: tools outside the institution's provision, including free public versions of commercial tools
tool_classes.ai_detection_tools: services that check text for AI or similarity, when the statement is about whether people may use or submit work to them
tool_classes.writing_and_translation_tools: grammar checkers, paraphrasing or rewriting tools and translation software
tool_classes.agentic_tools: AI agents, agentic browsers and tools that act for the user

tool_stances.provided: the institution supplies or licenses it
tool_stances.recommended: the institution recommends or prefers it
tool_stances.conditional: allowed only on a stated condition
tool_stances.not_endorsed: the institution does not recommend, endorse or vouch for it, without prohibiting it
tool_stances.warned: the document warns of risks or lost protections without a rule

data_types.own_work: the user's own work, drafts or ideas, including intellectual property in them
data_types.others_work_and_copyright: work created by others, copyright-protected material or licensed content
data_types.university_materials: university-owned or university-sensitive material such as slides, recordings, teaching materials and internal documents
data_types.student_work: work submitted by students, such as assignments and assessments
data_types.confidential_or_client_data: confidential institutional information, client data or information held under a non-disclosure agreement
data_types.research_data: research participant data, unpublished research or peer-review material
data_types.assessment_material: assessment briefs, exam papers, marking schemes or answer keys
data_types.credentials_or_accounts: passwords, login details or access to institutional accounts

data_stances.prohibited: may not be entered, uploaded or shared with AI tools
data_stances.conditional: may be entered only on a stated condition
data_stances.warned: the document warns of risk without a rule
data_stances.permitted: may be entered, with no condition stated

conditions.needs_permission: needs permission or consent (from staff, the owner or the person concerned)
conditions.anonymised: only if anonymised or stripped of identifying detail
conditions.approved_tool_only: only in an approved or institutional tool
conditions.meets_security_policy: only where the tool meets the institution's security, privacy or data protection requirements
conditions.risk_tiered: depends on a risk or sensitivity classification of the data

safeguards.check_terms_and_privacy: check a tool's terms of use, privacy settings or data practices before using it
safeguards.opt_out_of_training: opt out of, or protect work from, use of inputs to train models
safeguards.use_institutional_account: sign in with an institutional account or use an institution-managed version
safeguards.anonymise_before_entry: remove identifying detail before entering material
safeguards.follow_data_protection_policy: apply the institution's data protection, privacy or information security policy
safeguards.training_on_user_work_restricted: a statement that student or user work must not be used to train models without consent (a rule for the institution or vendors)

legal.terms_of_service: a tool's licence or terms of service
